Items.Authors: Arturo Osorio
Items.Title: Compact AO system for Cassegrain Telescopes: design and implementation for a 50 cm aperture
Items.Abstract: We present the optical design and implementation of a compact adaptive optics system to be mounted on small Cassegrain telescopes, particularly a 50cm telescope used at the SEETRUE Optical Grund Station located in Valparaiso, Chile. This compact design allows us to operate a robotic mount without a significant weight increment along with our 50cm Ritchey Chretien telescope. By using an off-the-shelf piezo electric deformable mirror and a custom non-modulated pyramid wavefront sensor, our system enables real-time tip/tilt correction as well as aberrations up to the first 37 Zernike modes when closing the adaptive optics loop while observing stars affected atmospheric turbulence. In this work we describe the optical design, passive and active optical elements, hardware and software used for real time control. At the moment the system is being implemented and has been tested on the optical bench with an emulated telescope.

Items.Authors: Makoto Yoshihara, Yusuke Yoshida, Yamato Ishida, Kazuki Ampuku, Koki Sakuta, Keitoku Yoshihira, Tetuo Kano, Naoki Ishida, Yoichi Yatsu, Yoshizumi Miyoshi, Kazushi Asamura, Noriko Yamasaki, Toru Tamagawa, Noriyuki Narukage, Yoshitaka Inoue, Takashi Okajima, Keisuke Tamura, Kikuko Miyata, Gota Yamaguchi, Shutaro Mohri, Takehiro Kume, Yusuke Matsuzawa, Yoichi Imamura, Takahiro Saito, Kentaro Hiraguri, Hirokazu Hashizume, Hidekazu Mimura, Ikuyuki Mitsuishi
Items.Title: Compact, high-sensitivity X-ray imaging spectroscopic instruments for CubeSats: development status
Items.Abstract: We have been developing a compact high-sensitivity X-ray imaging spectroscopic instrument for CubeSats. We have two optics designs: 100mm and 250mm in focal length, for 6U and 500mm-class CubeSats. Currently, we have completed the conceptual designs of our instruments, and a prototype was actually fabricated.   For the prototype instrument with two sample mirrors (φ20 and 40mm), we conducted the vibration tests in the z-axis direction for the first time. We applied the vibration level required for a sounding rocket. Consequently, no significant changes were observed through visual inspection. Furthermore, to quantitatively evaluate the load on the mirrors, we focused on the vibration response of the mirrors and confirmed resonance frequencies at 330 and 500 Hz corresponding to bending modes. These modes contribute more than two-thirds of the total load. In this presentation, the status of scientific feasibility study and instrument development will be reported.

Items.Authors: Yamato Ishida, Yusuke Yoshida, Makoto Yoshihara, Koki Sakuta, Kazuki Ampuku, Keitoku Yoshihira, Tetsuo Kano, Naoki Ishida, Yoichi Yatsu, Yoshizumi Miyoshi, Kazushi Asamura, Noriko Yamasaki, Toru Tamagawa, Noriyuki Narukage, Yoshitaka Inoue, Takashi Okajima, Keisuke Tamura, Kikuko Miyata, Gota Yamaguchi, Shutaro Mohri, Takehiro Kume, Yusuke Matsuzawa, Yoichi Imamura, Takahiro Saito, Kentaro Hiraguri, Hirokazu Hashizume, Hidekazu Mimura, Ikuyuki Mitsuishi
Items.Title: Compact, high-sensitivity X-ray imaging spectroscopic instruments for CubeSats: simulations
Items.Abstract: We are developing a compact high-sensitivity X-ray imaging spectroscopic instrument for small spacecraft such as CubeSats. Assuming a 6U CubeSat (100×200×300 mm), we conducted simulations based on a nested Wolter type-I mirror design with a focal length of 100 mm, total length of 100 mm, and apertures of 5, 10, and 20 mm. As a result, the imaging performance degraded more rapidly than in long-focal-length systems even when only geometric aberrations were considered, reaching HPD~50″ at an off-axis angle of 10′ at 1 keV. The HPD value also depended on an aperture size: at a 10′ off-axis angle, 5 mm and 20 mm single mirrors exhibited HPDs of ~300″ and ~30″, respectively. In addition, a stray light component specific to nested structures, such as backside reflections, appeared beyond 30′ off-axis. This poster presents these results for the 100-mm focal-length system and also results for 500×500×500 mm-class CubeSats.

Items.Authors: Alessandro Meoli, Olaf Iwert, Omar Sqalli, Mathias Richerzhagen, Elizabeth George, Matthias Seidel, Alexander Rüde
Items.Title: Conceptual architecture of the detector infrastructure for WST
Items.Abstract: The Wide-field Spectroscopic Telescope (WST) is a proposed 12 m wide-field spectroscopic facility combining several multi-object spectrographs. It requires a yet unprecedented number of detectors. In this paper we present a conceptual architecture for the detector controller and infrastructure required to operate a large number of detectors, potentially applicable to WST, focusing on the system-level, power distribution, and the associated data handling. We also consider how these elements may evolve over the expected development timeline of such a facility.  Motivated by the scale of the problem, we outline a possible distributed detector-controller architecture, based on modular units placed close to the detectors and networked backend electronics.

Items.Authors: William Schoenell, Christoph Birk, Jason Williams, Nick Konidaris, Paulo H. S. Silva
Items.Title: Control architecture for Henrietta spectrograph on the Swope Telescope
Items.Abstract: This presentation describes the development of the Henrietta instrument control software and its integration with the Swope TCS at Las Campanas Observatory, Chile. Henrietta is a near-infrared, low-resolution spectrograph designed for the Swope telescope, which has recently undergone significant technological upgrades. To unify this heterogeneous environment, we employed the Chimera Observatory Control System (OCS) to create standardized interfaces for all isolated components. This high-level integration enables control algorithms, such as observation scheduling, and weather safety, to operate independently of the underlying hardware, promoting flexibility and scalability. By establishing well-defined hardware interfaces, our approach facilitates the reuse of software components across different observatories and instruments. We discuss the implementation process, challenges encountered, and the broader impact of adopting Chimera OCS for observatory automation and interoperability.

Items.Authors: Owain Snaith, Narsireddy Anugu, Dan Lancaster, Stefan Kraus, Sebastien Morel, Mike Ireland, Jyotirmay Paul, Sorabh Chhabra
Items.Title: Control software framework for BIFROST, a 4-telescope J- and H-band interferometer for VLTI
Items.Abstract: BIFROST is part of the Asgard suite and is a 4-telescope interferometer in the J- and H-bands. BIFROST will be installed at the VLTI as a visitor instrument early in 2026. We will discuss the software framework for BIFROST and outline how we manage communications from different parts of Asgard, and the interaction of the various actuators and detectors during setup and observations. The final design of BIFROST will include two computers running Linux and numerous subsystems, including a group delay tracker, fibre explorer, real time display etc., which are required to conduct observations. BIFROST will interact with other parts of Asgard, and with a ESO compliant gateway computer running the VLTI observing software. Our software framework builds upon the software currently running MIRCX at CHARA and allows us to control two C-RED One near infrared cameras. The software is designed to be used via several remote GUIs, and via observing templates.

Items.Authors: Linbo Cao, Jinxin Liu, He Sun
Items.Title: Coronagraph as a spectrograph
Items.Abstract: Spectroscopic characterization is crucial for understanding stellar properties and for accurately calibrating the spectral differences between reference and target stars, which is essential for precise Point Spread Function (PSF) subtraction. However, many telescopes are not equipped with dedicated spectrographs for such characterization. In this presentation, we show a coronagraph can act as a low-resolution spectrometer: its wavelength-dependent modulation imprints spectral information onto the broadband coronagraphic PSF. We cast spectrum recovery as an inverse problem by fitting a forward PSF model to a single broadband image. Simulations and a laboratory demonstrator confirm feasibility, and we demonstrate the method on HST coronagraph data. This enables spectral inference from archival coronagraph images and relaxes color-matching constraints for PSF reference stars in future telescopes.

Items.Authors: Eduardo A. Bendek, Rachel E. Morgan, Dan Sirbu, Jon Lin, Ruslan Belikov
Items.Title: Coupling free space light into the AstroPIC photonic coronagraph
Items.Abstract: The Habitable Worlds Observatory (HWO) requires an unprecedented contrast of 1e-10 to characterize Exo-Earth atmospheres. Conventional free-space optics struggle with the stability and wavefront error correction needed for this high-contrast imaging, jeopardizing the mission’s exoplanet yield. Integrated photonics (PICs) offer a critical solution, providing superior stability, control, and compactness to boost coronagraph performance.  However, efficiently injecting light collected from the free-space telescope into the micron-scale PIC remains a major technical hurdle that directly limits system throughput. At NASA Ames, the AstroPIC laboratory is dedicated to optimize this injection efficiency. Our research progresses from single-fiber coupling to using a microlens arrays to maximize fill factor. Future efforts include utilizing wavefront information derived from the photonic coronagraph to drive a deformable mirror for active injection optimization into the PIC

Items.Authors: Domingo Alvarez Mendez, Oliver Pfuhl, Diego Del Valle, Christopher Mandla, Leander Mehrgan, Christophe Moins, Allar Saviauk, Mirko Todorovic
Items.Title: C-RED1 to FREDA: preparing infrared e-APD cameras for ESO AO systems
Items.Abstract: ESO is upgrading commercial C-RED1 e-APD cameras into ELT-compliant FREDA units for adaptive optics wavefront sensing. These cameras use 10 GbE RTMS pixel streaming for deterministic, multicast-capable data delivery, together with a PTP-synchronised control link that ensures precise timing within the ELT real-time architecture. Mechanical and thermal behaviour has been evaluated to confirm compliance with ELT operational constraints. A dedicated testbench applies harmonized characterization procedures across all FREDA units, covering detector gain, noise, dark current, linearity, and high-speed readout performance. Currently available optical configurations are assessed at an overview level to ensure compatibility with ELT and VLT instrument passbands. First results and the validation strategy will be presented, demonstrating how the FREDA transformation provides robust, interoperable, AO-optimized infrared detectors for next-generation systems.

Items.Authors: Davide Sisana, Bianca Salmaso, Daniele Spiga, Stefano Basso, Akanshu Chauhan, Simone Marini, Mauro Ghigo, Gabriele Vecchi, Giorgia Sironi, Giovanni Pareschi, Gianpiero Tagliaferri, Claudio Ferrari, Elena Ferrari, Manuel Sanchez del Rio, Marcos Bavdaz
Items.Title: Critical aspects in the development of the 1.49 keV channel for the BEaTriX X-ray calibration facility
Items.Abstract: BEaTriX is a compact X-ray facility operated at the INAF-OAB to test the NewAthena SPO MMs. It has two energy channels: the 4.51 keV beamline (operative) and the 1.49 keV (under development). The 1.49 keV channel presents more challenging aspects. We adopted a system based on two asymmetrically cut Quartz (10-10) crystals for the monochromator and two asymmetrically cut organic ADP (Ammonium Dihydrogen Phosphate) (101) crystals for the horizontal beam expansion stage. A particular emphasis was placed on the measurement of the planarity of internal lattice planes, as the requirements are very tight. Measurements performed at the diffractometer at IMEM-CNR and at the ESRF synchrotron revealed that the instrument's capabilities were approaching their limits, thereby highlighting previously unidentified systematic errors. The impact was simulated using both OASYS-SHADOW4 software and IDL reference code.

Items.Authors: Andrea Occhiuzzi, Luca Lamagna, Kentaro Kikuno, Tomotake Matsumura, Yutaro Sekimoto, Hayato Takakura, Giulia Barbieri Ripamonti, Elia Battistelli, Paolo de Bernardis, Federico Cacciotti, Fabio Columbro, Alessandro Coppolecchia, Marco De Petris, Elisabetta Marchitelli, Silvia Masi, Silvia Micheli, Mahdi Najafi, Alessandro Paiella, Francesco Piacentini, Giampaolo Pisano, Simone Stellati
Items.Title: Cryogenic measurements of the optical properties of microwave absorbers for the LiteBIRD telescope
Items.Abstract: Microwave absorbers suitable for cryogenic environments play a critical role in mitigating straylight within the telescope of the next-generation CMB satellite LiteBIRD. The stringent constraints on the mission’s mass budget, together with the requirements on residual reflectance and thermal performance at low temperatures, motivate the investigation of several mixtures of epoxy resins combined with different loading materials to identify the optimal recipes.   Preliminary cryogenic measurements were carried out using two low-temperature setups enabling the characterization of the samples down to 77 K and 4 K. The study focuses on the measurements of refractive index, loss tangent and specular reflectance in the 30–500 GHz frequency range, assessing how cryogenic operation affects the electromagnetic behavior of the materials. In parallel, a dedicated testbed for the measurement of the thermal contraction of the absorber candidates is currently under development at Sapienza University.

Items.Authors: Matteo Porru, Guido Cupani, Andrea Scaudo, Giorgio Calderone, Rodolfo Smiljanic, Mariagrazia Franchini, Roberto Cirami, Paolo Di Marcantonio, Matteo Genoni
Items.Title: CUBES software development in Active Flexure Compensation, E2E simulator and Data Reduction
Items.Abstract: CUBES (Cassegrain U-Band Efficient Spectrograph) is a high-efficiency spectrograph designed for the ESO VLT, targeting the near-UV wavelength range (300-405 nm) with spectral resolving powers of R=20,000 (high resolution) and R=7,000 (low resolution). CUBES recently completed its Final Design Review and entered the Manufacturing, Assembly, Integration, and Testing phase. This paper presents recent improvements in the Active Flexure Compensation (AFC) system, the End-to-End (E2E) simulator, and the Data Reduction Software (DRS).

Items.Authors: Shinji Fujita, Kenichi Karatsu, Shiro Ikeda, Akio Taniguchi, Akira Endo, Tatsuya Takekoshi, Yuri Nishimura, Kotaro Kohno, Stefanie A. Brackenhoff, Arend Moerman, Juri Yamanaka, Yoichi Tamura
Items.Title: Data processing and calibration pipeline for DESHIMA 2.0 observations on the ASTE telescope
Items.Abstract: Microwave kinetic inductance detectors (MKIDs) enable multiplexed spectroscopy at submillimeter wavelengths. DESHIMA 2.0, an on-chip filterbank spectrometer on the 10-m ASTE telescope in Chile, is among the first instruments to demonstrate wideband MKID spectroscopy on sky. While it provides simultaneous spectra over a broad band, the data require careful processing.  The responsivity and noise of individual KIDs vary between days due to atmospheric and instrumental conditions. Detector flagging, performance tracking, and calibration are essential. Atmospheric correction, responsivity normalization, and frequency alignment are required to convert raw timestreams into usable spectra or maps.  In this poster, we present the DESHIMA 2.0 data-processing workflow, including detector checks, automated masking, and calibration. We show how these procedures improve the fidelity and reproducibility of the final data and discuss implications for future DESHIMA and TIFUUN observations.

Items.Authors: Alexander M. Lapuente, Peter S. Barry, Chris Benson, Matt Bradford, Thomas Brien, Simon Doyle, Victor Gómez-Rivera, Jesús Hernández-Aguilar, José Luis Hérnandez-Rebollar, David H. Hughes, Elijah Kane, Kirit S. Karkare, Ryan McGeehan, Raúl Naranjo-Romero, Andreas Papageorgiou, Joseph Redford, Iván Rodríguez-Montoya, Sam Rowe, David Sánchez-Arguelles, Sofia Savorgnano, Annie Tan, Marcial Tapia, Jair Vega-Méndez, Steven Hailey-Dunsheath
Items.Title: Data reduction pipeline for the SuMaC millimeter-wave spectrometer at the LMT
Items.Abstract: We present the data reduction and analysis pipeline for the SuperSpec-MUSCAT Collaboration (SuMaC) along with several key science data products. In Summer 2025, SuperSpec on-chip spectrometers operating from 190-300 GHz at R~200 were deployed on the MUSCAT focal plane at the Large Millimeter Telescope (LMT), obtaining several days of high-quality on-sky data. Analysis of these data has been used to characterize noise performance and study spectra of various astrophysical sources, establishing the instrument’s viability for future line intensity mapping (LIM) deployments. We discuss calibration methods, data processing options, and preliminary analysis of the observed sources.

Items.Authors: Simone Doniselli, Edoardo Redaelli, Matteo Aliverti
Items.Title: Dealing with FREDA-induced vibrations in AO systems
Items.Abstract: The FREDA camera offers an autonomous cryogenic alternative to traditional liquid-nitrogen cooling for NIR detectors, simplifying operations through an integrated pulse-tube cryocooler and self-managed vacuum system. However, pulse-tube cooling can introduce mechanical vibrations that affect sensitive adaptive optics subsystems. This work presents a method to characterize and quantify these vibrations on the NGS wavefront sensors of the VLT/MAVIS and ELT/MORFEO instruments. The results support the development of mitigation strategies and guide the integration of autonomous cryogenic detectors into high-performance AO systems.

Items.Authors: Kenshi Yanagisawa, Riku Sato, Shinobu Ozaki, Chihiro Tokoku, Takashi Moriya, Kensho Tanaka, Tomoya Yukino, Kentaro Motohara, Yoshito Ono, Yosuke Minowa, Koki Terao, Kumiko Morihana, Yuki Moritani, Kosuke Kushibiki, Masami Ouchi, Nozomu Tominaga, Masayuki Tanaka, Yutaka Hayano, Yusei Koyama, Sadman Ali, Masaomi Tanaka, Masayuki Akiyama, Tohru Nagao, Yoshiki Matsuoka, Michitoshi Yoshida
Items.Title: Defective-pixel compensation for an infrared array detector in the NINJA echelle spectrograph
Items.Abstract: We present a defective-pixel compensation method for the infrared detector in NINJA, a LTAO-assisted, wide-band, high-sensitivity echelle spectrograph for the Subaru Telescope. The HAWAII-2RG detector exhibits ~10% defective pixels in its central region, requiring recovery of missing wavelength–intensity information. NINJA employs a detector-slide technique, mechanically shifting the detector along the dispersion direction to acquire multiple spectral images, which are then combined to reconstruct the missing data. For point sources, multi-position nodding can also recover missing pixels, but this is unsuitable for extended objects. The slide mechanism provides 0.3-pixel repeatability, less than 10% of the slit-image width, allowing reduced calibration frequency. An internal LED flat-field source further minimizes inter-pixel sensitivity calibration. We describe the implementation and expected performance of this approach.

Items.Authors: Kiumars Aryana, Gregory C. Jaehnig, Jason E. Austermann, James A. Beall, Matthew A. Koc, Shannon M. Duff, Jeff van Lanen, Kevin C. Cossel, John H. Lehman, Johannes Hubmayr, Solomon I. Woods, Adam J. Fleisher
Items.Title: Demonstration of long-wave infrared Virtually Imaged Phased Array (VIPA)
Items.Abstract: Earth-like planets emit thermal radiation predominantly in the mid- to far-infrared, spanning roughly 4 μm to 100 μm, with a peak near 11 μm. Despite the scientific importance of this spectral region for habitable world surveys, there are currently very few spectrometers capable of operating in this regime. To address this gap, we present the design, fabrication, and experimental characterization of an air-gapped, silicon-based virtually imaged phased array (VIPA) optimized for mid-IR spectroscopy. The device consists of a 1″ wide, 3″ tall high-purity silicon plate pair with two coating configurations, gold (Au) and titanium nitride (TiN). Using quantum cascade lasers at wavelengths of 14 μm and 17 μm, paired with a THz microbolometer detector array, we characterize the VIPA’s dispersion and evaluate its resolving power. We also develop computational models to simulate the VIPA’s dispersion and expected resolving power, enabling direct comparison with the measured performance.

Items.Authors: Mashakanya Mashiloane, Humphrey Matlala, Vusani Mbobvu, Mpendulo Ndelane, Lucia Salukazana, Simisi Mosamane, Rofhiwa Takalani
Items.Title: Deployment of sustainable microgrid architectures for radio telescope antennas at SKA-MID
Items.Abstract: The Square Kilometre Array Observatory (SKAO) plans to deploy microgrid power supply architectures for electrifying selected remote telescope antennas at its SKA-Mid site in the Karoo. Whilst the deployment of microgrid systems is not a new concept for electrical power provision, SKAO seeks to align this deployment with its sustainability goals.  This paper discusses different microgrid architectures that SKA-Mid could deploy, considering SKAO’s sustainability goals, the environment at the Karoo site and South Africa’s energy resource landscape. The paper recommends sustainable microgrid architectures that can be deployed at SKA-Mid based on the site’s environmental impact,  sustainable power sources availability and economics.

Items.Authors: Pablo Strazzeri, Eduardo Carella, Néstor Del Castillo, Gabriel De Innocenti, Gustavo Domínguez, Alberto Etchegoyen, Luciano Ferreyro, Juan Geria, Daniel Gorbeña, Laurent Grandsire, Matías Hampel, Facundo Lazarte, Alexis Mancilla, Javier Maya, Julio Migliori, Hernán Ocampo, Andrés Pantarotto, Manuel Platino, Emiliano Rasztocky, Adrián Riello, Cristian Rodríguez, Fabricio Rodríguez, Diego Silva, Alejando Solís, Lucía Sucunza, Carlos Varela
Items.Title: Design and construction of the QUBIC instrument mount
Items.Abstract: The Q & U Bolometric Interferometer for Cosmology (QUBIC) is a novel polarimeter optimized for measuring the B-mode polarization of the Cosmic Microwave Background (CMB). The instrument combines two complementary techniques: it uses interferometry to achieve excellent control of instrumental systematic effects, and bolometric detection to obtain high sensitivity.   This work presents the design, construction, and testing of the mount that supports the instrument and enables its motion. The mount features three rotational axes, azimuth, elevation, and boresight. Although the main science target is a small region of the sky, the instrument must be capable of rotating more than 360° in azimuth in order to point toward a calibration source located on the opposite side of the observable sky.

Items.Authors: Mario Nicola Mazziotta
Items.Title: Design and construction of the segmented plastic scintillator SiPM-readout anti-coincidence detector for ADAPT
Items.Abstract: The Antarctic Demonstrator for the Advanced Particle-astrophysics Telescope (ADAPT) is a NASA suborbital mission for a high-altitude balloon flight over Antarctica, which is anticipated to fly in the 2026-27 season. ADAPT validates key technologies for the future space-based APT, which aims for an order of magnitude improvement in MeV-TeV gamma-ray sensitivity.    This presentation details the Design and Construction of the ADAPT Anti-Coincidence Detector (ACD). The ACD is critical for achieving high-efficiency charged particle veto, selecting gamma-ray candidate events from the overwhelming cosmic-ray background. The detector uses segmented plastic scintillator tiles read out by Silicon Photomultipliers (SiPMs). We will detail the fabrication process and present early performance metrics, including light yield measurements, validating the ACD as a high-performance pathfinder for the full APT mission.

Items.Authors: Arijit Maiti, Bhavesh Kumar Mistry, Mudit K. Srivastava
Items.Title: Design and development of a Prototype Integral Field Unit (Proto-IFU) for PRL 2.5m telescope
Items.Abstract: Proto-IFU is an optical-fibre-based Integral Field Unit (IFU) which is being developed as a prototype subsystem to add two-dimensional spectroscopic capabilities to a low-resolution long-slit spectrograph. It is based on the concept of coupling the telescope focal plane with the spectrograph slit using a lenslet array + fibre unit assembly, to sample the incoming field of view spatially. A 2D matrix pinhole array at the input and a V-groove array at the output reroute the optical fibres from a 2D field to a 1D slit, which gets re-imaged on the spectrograph slit. Optimized for the visible spectrum, Proto-IFU offers spatial sampling scales of 0.75 arc-seconds per fibre, providing a field of view of 7.5 × 7.5 arc-seconds squared on the sky. In this proposed poster, the speaker shall demonstrate the design, development, and laboratory characterization of the instrument.

Items.Authors: Aditya Garde, Roland den Hartog, Henk Hoevers, Matthijs Langelaar, Just Herder
Items.Title: Design and development of an X-ray interferometry testbed
Items.Abstract: X-ray Interferometry(XRI) has the potential for ultra-high resolution imaging. The XRI design by Willingale allows the interferometer to be compact enough to fit in a single spacecraft. The approach has been tested in visible wavelength however, is yet to be tested with X-rays. Here we report on the design and the current status of the XRI testbed. We are currently building an facility at SRON to test the Willingale XRI. The facility will allow testing of a 1cm baseline XRI at 1.25keV. The testbed consists a rotating anode X-ray source. A slit mechanism is placed in front to have a spatially coherent beam. Further, it has a 15m long vacuum line including a vacuum chamber which houses an optical bench to mount the optics. The optics consists 3 flat mirrors and a slatted mirror fabricated by cosine. Mirrors are placed at grazing incidence with alignment mechanisms. The fringes will be detected by a CMOS. The development will serve as a platform for testing current and future XRI designs.

Items.Authors: Patrick Ashworth, Peter Barry, Chris Benson, Karia Dibert, Harry Gordon-Moys, Kirit Karkare, Annie Tan, Izaak Morris
Items.Title: Design and fabrication of a high-resolution superconducting silicon vacuum waveguide spectrometer
Items.Abstract: We present a prototype device using micromachined silicon waveguides, coated with superconducting niobium. A simple channelising filter-bank composed of single pole iris-coupled cavity resonators disperses the incident light, with each spectral channel coupled to an in-plane waveguide that enables efficient, straightforward detector integration. Implementing detailed electromagnetic simulations, we report the design, optimisation, and fabrication of a small-scale prototype R = 500 waveguide spectrometer based on the standard WR3 geometry operating across the 1 mm (220–310 GHz) atmospheric window.

Items.Authors: Youming Guo, Lingxiao Li, Zibo Ke
Items.Title: Design and implementation of a 4.2-m telescope adaptive optics system for solar system object observations and laser guide star performance testing
Items.Abstract: A spatiotemporal reference frame underpins human activity and science. The 4.2-m ground-based astrometric telescope will maintain high-precision Solar System ephemerides by tracking the orbits of planets, dwarf planets, satellites, and asteroids for space missions. Atmospheric turbulence limits large apertures, so adaptive optics (AO) is required for high resolution. To enable both narrow- and wide-field observing, we will develop conventional AO for near diffraction-limited imaging in narrow fields and ground-layer AO (GLAO) for wide fields. GLAO targets dominant near-ground turbulence: multiple sodium laser guide stars sample different directions and drive ground-layer wavefront correction, improving seeing over a larger field. A deformable secondary mirror will simplify the system, reduce residual wavefront error, and increase throughput and sky coverage. R&D covers sodium beacon lasers, multi-LGS wavefront sensing, high-density deformable secondaries, and wavefront control overall

Items.Authors: Thomas Schweizer, Josef Eder, Holger Wetteskind, Christopher Jablonski, Robert Stadler, Masahiro Teshima, Razmik Mirzoyan, Armand Fiasson, Guilaume Deleglise, Nicolas Geffroy, Rafael Garcia, Julia Mundet
Items.Title: Design and realisation of the 23m diameter LST mechanical structure for the Cherenkov Telescope Array
Items.Abstract: The 23m diameter Large Size Cherenkov Telescope (LST) for CTA on the Canary Island La Palma 2250 m asl is the next generation Cherenkov telescope after MAGIC, H.E.S.S. and VERITAS. In order to allow rapid repositioning (180deg in 18sec) for gamma ray bursts, the mechanical structure has been designed to be ultra-light weight (110tons). The space frame structure is composed of slender struts (carbon fibre, aluminum (dish & camera mast) as well as steel). The main structure withstands extremely high wind speeds (<200km/h), uplift and ice formation (<30tons) as typical at the observatory ORM in La Palma. Here we present the specific design to comply with the functional and environmental requirements The MPP, Munich is responsible for the mechanical structure of the telescope together with partner institutes from France (LAPP) and Spain (IFAE). The prototype LST1 has been installed and is operational since 2019. Three more LST´s are presently under construction.

Items.Authors: Laney Saye, John Groh, Tran Tsan
Items.Title: Design and validation of a generalized cooldown simulation tool for cryogenic millimeter-wave telescopes
Items.Abstract: Modern, large-format cryogenic cameras for mm-wave and sub-mm cosmology, including CMB experiments, require multi-stage cryogenic systems for sensitive detector operation. As these cameras increase in size, cooldown time can become prohibitively long. To address this and allow for valuable comparative studies early in the design process, we developed a thermal simulation tool to predict cooldown timelines and heat flows. Our model is flexible to various geometries and does not rely on final-stage design. Unlike previous cryogenic thermal network models, it incorporates thermal loading through the mm-transparent window and its associated infrared filters. We validate our tool against published cooldown thermometer data from a pulse-tube cooled ground-based CMB telescope, replicating the overall cooldown duration to ~25% accuracy and reproducing most qualitative features of the cooldown profile. We plan to release the code publicly for general use.

Items.Authors: Shi-hao Lu, Hong-fei Zhang, Jian Wang, Hao-ran Ma
Items.Title: Design of a compact scientific CCD camera with EMI suppression
Items.Abstract: This paper presents the design of a compact, scientific - grade CCD camera utilizing a 1K*1K pixels sensor and a Thermoelectric Cooler (TEC). To achieve a balance between a compact form factor and low readout noise, the design incorporates a modular architecture comprising a front - amplifier, power supply, driver, and main control board, along with an analog baseline restoration circuit. Crucially, a dedicated TEC driver board with advanced electromagnetic interference (EMI) suppression is implemented to mitigate the switching noise inherent in the cooling process.  Experimental results demonstrate that the system achieves excellent low-noise performance and thermal stability, validating the effectiveness of the proposed miniaturization and EMI suppression strategies.

Items.Authors: Shuo Wang, Qihang Zhang, Shuangquan Chen, Yonggang Gu, Chao Zhai
Items.Title: Design of a next-generation fiber optic positioning unit drive system
Items.Abstract: In order to advance the LAMOST Phase II project, this paper aims to design a motor drive system based on STM32. First, a PCB drive board with a simpler structure and richer functionality was designed using Cadence Allegro, and components were reselected. Second, based on the Keil development software, a rigorous communication program was designed according to the instructions from the host computer, including processes such as data frame transmission and reception handling, two-step operation, and error feedback mechanisms. At the same time, a new drive program was redesigned, utilizing an 'S-shaped' acceleration and deceleration curve for smooth start and stop, allowing the motor to start and stop at any phase, and replacing full-step driving with microstepping. Experimental results show that the drive board has a compact structure and complete functions; the software program can meet the expected requirements.

Items.Authors: Peter P. Pedersen, Clark E. Baker, Karolina Dziewiecka, Mathias Beck, Didier Queloz
Items.Title: Design of a simultaneous InGaAs–CCD split-beam imager for ultra-cool dwarf exoplanet transit survey
Items.Abstract: We present the design and development of a new dual-channel imager for the SPECULOOS Southern Observatory (SSO) dedicated to detecting and characterizing transiting exoplanets orbiting ultra-cool dwarfs. The instrument will enable simultaneous visible and near-infrared observations by splitting the beam at 955 nm between silicon based CCD and CMOS based InGaAs detectors. Simultaneous dual-band photometry will aid disentangling stellar variability signals—spots and faculae—from planetary transits. Filter choices for the near-infrared channels are chosen to mitigate atmospheric PWV variability, improving transit detection precision. We describe the opto-mechanical design, filter and detector selection. The instrument design is expected on-sky in early 2027 on two 1-meter class SSO telescopes.

Items.Authors: Kosuke Kushibiki, Shinobu Ozaki, Toshihiro Tsuzuki, Yutaka Yamagata, Takuya Hosobata, Masahiro Takeda, Shinya Morita, Keiichi Nakagawa, Yuki Inada, Kentaro Motohara, Hidenori Takahashi, Masahiro Konishi, Natsuko Kato, Jeung Yun, Akino Yasuda, Tomoya Yukino, Misato Fujii, Kensho Tanaka, Taiki Kikuchi
Items.Title: Design of an image-slicer integral field unit with free-form mirrors for a near-infrared spectrograph SWIMS
Items.Abstract: SWIMS-IFU is an image-slicer-type integral field unit (IFU) for a near-infrared imager and spectrograph SWIMS, one of the first-generation instruments for the TAO 6.5 m telescope. By optimizing a slice width to a typical seeing of 0.5″, SWIMS-IFU provides a wider field of view (FoV) of 17.17″ x 14.0″ compared with existing near-infrared integral field spectrographs.    Due to the limited volume of 235 mm x 170 mm x 55 mm allowed for the IFU, it turns out to be impossible to design an optical system using ordinary spherical mirrors without introducing significant aberrations. To overcome this issue, we have designed an optical system using multiple free-form mirrors. This design delivers nearly diffraction-limited performance at the image slicer. The complex mirror geometries will be realized using an ultra-precision cutting technique.    In this presentation, we will describe the specifications and details of the SWIMS-IFU optical design.

Items.Authors: Jie Hu, Zheng Lou, Wei Geng, Qiang Zhi, Zhi Li, Yutan Zhang, Jiameng Wang, Zhenhui Lin, Zheng Wang, Kangmin Zhou, Jing Li, Shengcai Shi
Items.Title: Design of multi-color large field of view camera for XSMT based on kinetic inductance detectors
Items.Abstract: In this presentation, we introduce the design of a wide-field kinetic inductance detector (KID) camera being developed for the 15-m XSMT Telescope, currently under construction in XueShanMuChang (96°35′08.6″ E, 37°58′36.2″ N; altitude 4,820 m), Qinghai, China. The instrument provides a 14″ field of view with an effective focal ratio of f/2.9 and operates simultaneously in three frequency bands centered at 230, 345, and 460 GHz. The two higher-frequency bands, 345 and 460 GHz, are on-chip diplexed and share a common focal plane, significantly reducing the complexity of both the cryogenic system and the optical design. As a result, the in-cryostat optics are simplified to a single dichroic and two mirrors, and the cryostat dimensions are reduced to approximately 0.8 m × 1.0 m × 0.8 m. The focal plane has a diameter of 190 mm and accommodates seven horn-coupled lumped-element KID arrays employing Hilbert-curve meanders. In total, the camera comprises approximately 8000 pixels.

Items.Authors: Juriy Hastanin, Emmanuel Mazy, Guilhem Terrasa, Alexandra Mazzoli, Colin Dandumont, Laurence Rossi, Jean-François Vandenrijt, Jean-Yves Plesseria, Marc P. Georges, Riccardo Gabrieli, Beatrice Tofani, Benedetta Talone
Items.Title: Design optimization of the Forward Baffle of the ESA Vigil Heliospheric Imager
Items.Abstract: Vigil is an upcoming ESA satellite mission designed to monitor space weather, with a particular focus on the solar corona and the interplanetary space between the Sun and Earth.  This paper introduces the basic design of a Forward Baffle (FB), currently being developed for the Heliospheric Imager (HI) instrument included in the Vigil spacecraft’s payload to observe very faint coronal mass ejections (CME) across a wide field of view.  The wide-angle FB is one of the key optical components of the HI designed to suppress direct stray-light from the solar disk. It consists of a multi-stage diffractive vanes (MSDV) module involving a pyramidal wedge structure with a high-reflectivity surface coating and a dedicated thermo-mechanically stabilized FB supporting assembly providing the required spatial and angular position of the MSDV relative to two observation cameras of the HI instrument. The FB supporting assembly is designed to meet the accommodation constrains of the HI instrument.

Items.Authors: Carlos Miravet, Gonzalo Taubmann, Isabel Soto, Janire Zabaleta, Eneko Reina, José María Arroyo, Natalia Eugenia de Burgos, Irune Jimenez, Claudia Bear, Jorge Mugica
Items.Title: Design, assembly, and test of a sun polychromator prototype for TRUTHS mission
Items.Abstract: The TRUTHS mission, led by ESA, aims to establish a reference standard for Earth’s radiative state, enabling SI-traceable calibration and improving climate data consistency. A key element of its On-Board Calibration System is the Solar Polychromator (SPC), a tuneable bandpass instrument that filters solar radiation across 320–2400 nm for high-accuracy spectral calibration.  This work presents the design and verification of a prototype SPC, developed to validate the optical concept before flight implementation. Laboratory tests using a monochromator assessed wavelength accuracy, spectral resolution (FWHM), and straylight suppression. Results show strong agreement between measured and predicted filtering behaviour, confirming accurate modelling and alignment. A Structural-Thermal-Optical Performance (STOP) analysis demonstrated stability under orbital thermal conditions.

Items.Authors: Archita Rai, Kyohoon Ahn, Jae Joon Lee
Items.Title: Design, implementation, and evaluation of a laboratory MOAO system
Items.Abstract: Adaptive optics (AO) is integral to the astronomical instrumentation landscape for all the leading large optical/IR telescope observatories. AO systems have been utilized to improve the astronomical seeing experienced by ground-based telescopes. The system compensates for the wavefront distortions in astronomical images due to the Earth’s atmospheric turbulence. Multi-object adaptive optics (MOAO) systems are a type of AO suitable for multi-object data retrieval (spectroscopy: MOS). The goal here is to secure a reasonably high Strehl ratio only for the specific region of interest, not for the full FoV. In this nature, the MOAO system uses multiple open-loop deformable mirrors correcting specific FoV in the direction of science objects. The loop configurations used in our system are open-loop and pseudo closed-loop using a Shack–Hartmann wavefront sensor (SH-WFS) to measure wavefront slopes across sub-apertures. We present the detailed aspects of MOAO systems.

Items.Authors: Andrea Orlati, Alessandro Scalambra, Matteo Fiorentini, Marco Poloni, Federico Perini, Adelaide Ladu, Luca Schirru
Items.Title: Design, implementation, and test of the intermediate frequency distribution system for the Sardinia Radio Telescope high-frequency multi-feed receivers
Items.Abstract: This paper presents the design and implementation of the new Intermediate Frequency Distribution (IFD) system for the Sardinia Radio Telescope (SRT). Developed for the telescope's upgrade to high-frequency bands, the IFD handles unprecedented bandwidths up to 18 GHz and high channel counts from new multi-feed receivers. The system ensures efficient signal routing from the receiver cabin to the digital backends in the control room. We detail the technical specifications derived from operational use cases and the custom architecture designed to integrate with the existing infrastructure. The study focuses on the technological solutions adopted for critical subsystems and presents comprehensive laboratory test results, demonstrating the system's essential role in enabling SRT’s advanced high-frequency capabilities.

Items.Authors: Nicola La Palombara, Gabriele Dal Ben, Simone Piras, Ilaria Dal Ben, Filippo Dal Ben, Julien Cailleux, Fatima De Frondat Laadim, Assia El Mouden, Luigi Lessio, Giuseppe Leto, Gino Tosti, Laura Proserpio, Salvatore Scuderi, Alessio Trois, Fulvio Gianotti, Ismam Abu, Gianpiero Tagliaferri
Items.Title: Design, manufacturing, and quality control of the mechanical structures of the Small Size Telescopes for CTAO
Items.Abstract: The Small-Size Telescopes (SSTs) of the Cherenkov Telescope Array Observatory (CTAO) are developed by an international consortium of institutes that will provide them as an in-kind contribution to CTAO.  Here we present the design and manufacturing phases of the mechanical structures of the SSTs. Since they are based on the heritage of the ASTRI telescopes, we describe how the original design of the ASTRI telescopes was modified, in order to improve the telescope performance, to host the SST Cherenkov camera, and to be compliant with the environmental, quality, interface, and safety requirements of CTAO. We also present the various phases of the manufacturing process, describing the details of each step, and the formal inspections performed along it. Finally, we discuss the Quality Control Matrix used to perform the quality check of each manufacturing phase, and describe in detail the various types of test applied to verify the correct execution of the welding and painting phases.

Items.Authors: Jin Xin Jesse Lin, Keith Vanderlinde
Items.Title: Design, systems integration and validation of focus electronics for the Canadian Hydrogen Observatory and Radio-transient Detector
Items.Abstract: Large-N radio arrays, featuring hundreds or thousands of receivers, require precise alignment while presenting problems of reproducibility, cost, and systems integration. In response, we aim for a repeatable, low-cost, and highly manufacturable design of focus electronics for the Canadian Hydrogen Observatory and Radio-Transient Detector (CHORD). This is achieved through a combination of laser cutting, machining, injection moulding and FDM 3D printing. Additionally, metrology on all components is completed to verify manufacturing consistency. In this paper, I will discuss the design decisions of the focus electronics and systems integration with the full CHORD receiver chain.

Items.Authors: Hillary H. Head, David C. Morris, Manuel Díaz Alfaro, Nuria Wright-Garba, Anthony Santini, Andres Parraguez, Alexandra Tritschler
Items.Title: Designing a document management tool in JIRA for Science Operations Specialists
Items.Abstract: The Science Operations Specialists at the National Science Foundation’s Daniel K. Inouye Solar Telescope developed an innovative use of Atlassian’s JIRA software as a documentation management tool. The primary objectives for creating this tool were to enhance team accessibility to the documentation workflow process, develop automation to ease the administrative and management task load, and enable supervisors to monitor documentation tasks in an optimized format. The team implemented this management system for both the procedural documentation involved with telescope operations as well as the knowledgebase and key concepts training documentation used in training new hires. Our overall documentation management system used Confluence as our documentation container and JIRA as our documentation process management and monitoring system. A predecessor Google Sheets tool defined the necessary content and provided a baseline for defining successful implementation within the JIRA space.

Items.Authors: Robin Anthony-Petersen, Steven E. Boggs, Emily Broadbent, Julian Gerber, Felix Hagemann, Sophia E. Haight, Dieter Hartmann, Carolyn A. Kierans, Matthew Lassiter, Alex Lowell, Brent Mochizuki, Samer Al Nussirat, Jarred Roberts, Parshad Patel, Nicole Rodriguez Cavero, Field Rogers, Clio C. Sleator, John A. Tomsick, Andreas Zoglauer
Items.Title: Detector-level calibrations for the COSI mission
Items.Abstract: Have you heard of the MeV gap? It’s the energy range between 0.1 and 30 MeV where our observing sensitivity is far lower than neighboring bands, yet where many extreme astrophysical phenomena can be studied. The Compton Spectrometer and Imager (COSI), a NASA Small Explorer mission launching in 2027, will observe the entire sky daily from 0.2–5 MeV with unprecedented sensitivity and excellent energy resolution (~0.5–1.2% FWHM), opening a new window into the soft gamma-ray sky. COSI’s main instrument consists of sixteen cross-strip high-purity germanium detectors. After fabrication, each detector undergoes extensive performance tests and detailed calibrations. Here we give an overview of COSI’s detectors, the testing setup, and the calibration efforts, which includes: energy, position, and timing calibration; studies of charge trapping and transport effects; measurements of detector deadtime; and the backend analysis pipeline.

Items.Authors: Lorenzo Merli, Daniele Vassallo, Alessandro Ballone, Luca Cortese, Guido Agapito, Fabio Rossi, Alfio Puglisi, Oleksandra Rebrysh, Simone Di Filippo, Valentina Viotto, Luca Marafatto, Carmelo Arcidiacono, Davide Greggio, Kalyan Radhakrishnan, Maria Bergomi
Items.Title: Developing a SPECULA-based digital twin MATTO test bench
Items.Abstract: MATTO (Multi-conjugate Adaptive Techniques Test Optics) is a wide field adaptive optics (AO) test bench currently under development at the INAF Astronomical Observatory of Padova. Its primary goal is to support the study and development of future multi-conjugate adaptive optics (MCAO) techniques.  The highly modular architecture enables MATTO to reproduce a broad variety of atmospheric conditions, optical configuration, and control strategies.  To validate the system’s design and support its calibration and performance optimization, we are developing a realistic numerical simulation to serve as a digital twin of the bench. The simulation is being built using SPECULA, a Python-based adaptive optics simulation package developed at INAF–Arcetri.  In this contribution, we present the structure of the MATTO digital twin, discuss the initial results obtained, and compare these outcomes with analytical performance predictions derived from the TipTop tool.

Items.Authors: Fabienne Mangelsdorff, Andreas Stoll, Kalaga Madhav, Martin M. Roth, Lars Zimmermann, Stefan Lischke, Riya Mary Pattery
Items.Title: Development concept for a Compact Arrayed Waveguide Stacked Multi-Object Spectrograph (CAWSMOS)
Items.Abstract: The linear size of a bulk optical astronomical spectrograph scales with the diameter of the primary mirror of the corresponding telescope. As modern telescopes continue to increase in aperture size, miniaturization of the spectrograph becomes crucial beyond the offered advantages in terms of multifunctional integration and photon efficiency.  The presented concept of development for a Compact Arrayed Waveguide Stacked Multi-Object Spectrograph (CAWSMOS) includes the design of the AWG chips, the stacking frame and cross-dispersion optics for the imaging of multiple spectral orders per AWG.  It aims to reduce the cost and size of astronomical spectrographs while also improving efficiency. This will bring the AWG technology closer to the realization of its full potential for ground based, airborne and spaceborne astronomical applications.

Items.Authors: Shogo Nohara, Kotaro Niinuma, Sogo Dan, Ayato Omori, Akira Kameyama, Kazuma Mukai, Hideo Ogawa, Naoto Sekiya, Keita Sakuma, Pang Yuhong, Yasumasa Yamasaki, Kei Amada, Kazuyoshi Sunada, Takuya Akahori, Tomoaki Oyama, Yutaka Hasegawa, Kohei Kurahara
Items.Title: Development of 6 – 18 GHz wideband cooled receiver for VERA
Items.Abstract: VLBI Exploration of Radio Astrometry (VERA) network has been attracting attention on follow-up observations of transient phenomenon. To understand the radiation mechanism of non-thermal emission from such transient phenomena, simultaneous wide-band observation at centimeter wavelengths is essential. The Cassegrain design of VERA demands a large feed horn for the centimeter band, requiring a single broadband receiver. Furthermore, the centimeter band is heavily impacted by radio frequency interference (RFI) from satellite transmission and industrial use.   Therefore, we are developing a 6 – 18 GHz receiver featuring, (1) insertion of a low-loss High-Temperature Superconductivity Filter before the first amplifier to selectively cut RFI, (2) adoption of a 6 – 18 GHz Quadruple-Ridged Horn Antenna, and (3) use of a lightweight and compact Stirling Cryocooler.   In this poster, we will report on the design and status of the cooling dewar and the development progress of the receiving system.

Items.Authors: Tomonori Ikeda
Items.Title: Development of a gaseous electron-tracking Compton camera with electron-recoil reconstruction using deep learning
Items.Abstract: MeV gamma-ray observations remain far less explored than the X-ray, GeV, and TeV bands, creating the well-known MeV gap. A major challenge in this energy range is the improvement of the point spread function (PSF) of Compton telescopes. The electron-tracking Compton camera (ETCC) is one of the most promising instruments to overcome this gap, as its PSF strongly depends on the accuracy of the reconstructed electron-recoil direction. To address this, we developed a deep-learning–based reconstruction method using track-imaging data. In particular, we implemented a reconstruction algorithm to estimate the three-dimensional electron-recoil direction from a two-dimensional image obtained with CCD-based optical readout of a gaseous time projection chamber. This approach has the potential to enable the development of a CCD-based gaseous ETCC and to enhance the PSF of future MeV gamma-ray telescopes.

Items.Authors: Antonio Nazareno Uchoa de Oliveira Filho, Rafael Alves de Souza Ribeiro, Alex Cavaliéri Carciofi, Tiago Giorgetti
Items.Title: Development of a high-precision polarimetry roadmap at IAG-USP
Items.Abstract: We present the progress of a phased development program to build a high-precision polarimeter at IAG-USP, targeting sensitivities of $10^{-5}$ to $10^{-6}$ for small and medium-sized telescopes. The project addresses the instrumental gap in the Southern Hemisphere for polarimetric science, including exoplanet characterization and stellar magnetic fields. The proposed roadmap seeks to accelerate in-house instrumentation development at the IAG-USP Optics Laboratory. The first phase focuses on a low-cost, compact prototype for the 50mm SeeStar S50 telescope, employing a dual-beam configuration with a rotating HWP and a fixed Wollaston prism, establishing a laboratory framework for future upgrades. We detail the optical modeling and key engineering trade-offs. Later phases will scale the instrument and incorporate faster modulators (FLCs/PEMs) and high-sensitivity detectors (PMTs/APDs) to reach the target precision, emphasizing a robust, low-noise polarimetric architecture.

Items.Authors: Daiki Ishi, Yoshitomo Maeda, Manabu Ishida, Asca Miyamoto, Atsuto Matsumura, Tsubasa Uchino
Items.Title: Development of a large-aperture x-ray irradiation system at the ISAS 30-m beam line facility
Items.Abstract: We present a large-aperture x-ray irradiation system developed at the 30-m beam line facility of the Institute of Space and Astronautical Science to enable faster and more flexible calibration of x-ray telescope modules. The system uses an uncollimated, naturally diverging beam from an x-ray generator, reaching 270 mm in diameter at 27 m from the source. Beam baffles suppress scattered x-rays, and a new quadrupole slit assembly defines an illuminated area up to 140 mm × 140 mm within the beam. Beam uniformity measurements with a large-format CMOS detector show spatial variations within 3% for Al and Cu characteristic-line targets. This system supports efficient end-to-end testing of small, lightweight telescope modules for upcoming missions.

Items.Authors: Gwendal Deniel, Jean-Pierre Thermeau, Michel Piat, Marie-Reine N'Sougan, Christophe Chailan, Laurent Grandsire, Alin Ilioni, Patxi Duthil, Rémy Thoër
Items.Title: Development of a platform dedicated to the measurement of material properties at cryogenic temperatures : CryoMat
Items.Abstract: The CryoMat project aims to answer a demand in the field of astrophysics, where instruments need to work at cryogenic temperatures to get high sensitivity. A wealth of data on the properties of metallic and plastic materials is now available for temperatures down to 1K. However, there is still a significant lack of data on thermal, electrical and mechanical properties, particularly for anisotropic materials, and especially composites, across the 1K – 300K temperature range, and below 1K for metallic and plastic materials.    CryoMat will aim to fill this gap by developing a platform dedicated to the characterization of materials at cryogenic temperatures, down to sub-Kelvin. This platform, based on the Grands Moulins campus of Université Paris Cité (Paris, France), will be accessible to scientific laboratories and industries. CryoMat will cover three families of physical properties installed in cryostats dedicated to electrical, thermal and mechanical properties.

Items.Authors: Chiara Scandaglia, Runa Briguglio, Matteo Menessini, Marco Xompero, Alberto Riva
Items.Title: Development of an integrated model of a high order, active segmented mirror for space telescopes
Items.Abstract: The scientific cases of interest for next-generation space telescopes result in challenging requirements for resolution, contrast and wavefront stability, which must be matched with an effective mission risk and cost mitigation. The integration of a deformable primary mirror with contactless actuators can address these needs by enabling active wavefront control, vibration rejection and weight reduction through the use of lighter materials.   The present work aims to provide a parametric integrated model to simulate the effects of the orbital environment on a space telescope equipped with an active segmented primary mirror. The simulator will compute thermal deformations on the support, disturbance propagation to the optics and the wavefront correction to deliver at the focal plane. Through a trade-off study of orbital and system parameters, the goal of the tool is to investigate the attractiveness of the contactless deformable mirror technology in terms of mission cost and performance.

Items.Authors: Kosuke Aizawa, Ryosuke Akizawa, Paolo de Bernardis, Francisco Javier Casas, Ilenia Di Nitto, Ricardo Tanausú Génova-Santos, Shotaro Kawano, Kuniaki Konishi, Luca Lamagna, Asuka Maeda, Enrique Martinez-Gonzalez, Silvia Masi, Tomotake Matsumura, Guillermo Pascual-Cisneros, Jose Alberto Rubino-Martin, Haruyuki Sakurai, Ryota Takaku
Items.Title: Development of anti-reflection sub-wavelength structures with laser ablation on sapphires for W-band CMB polarimetry
Items.Abstract: We present optical designs and performances of a sapphire half-wave plate (HWP) for W-band cosmic microwave background (CMB) polarimeters. We designed the HWP with a single layer sapphire with the anti-reflection sub-wavelength structures (SWS) patterned on a sapphire slab using 1030 nm lasers with 4 ps pulse duration and 40 W output power. We fabricated the 20 by 20 SWS array on an A-cut sapphire sample as a prototype demonstration. Based on the fabricated shape, the in-band averaged modulation efficiency and reflection are 93% and < 1%, respectively. The in-band transmittance is larger than 97% considering a loss tangent value of 4\times10^{-4}. We also further optimized the design by taking into account the convergence of the ray into the receiver. We introduce a HWP model to account for the effect of non-parallel rays on the birefringent material including the SWS layer.

Items.Authors: Rekhesh Mohan
Items.Title: Development of CubeSat based UV astronomy payloads at the Indian Institute of Astrophysics: launch opportunities and challenges
Items.Abstract: The space industry is experiencing a paradigm shift globally and within India. There is a widespread interest in CubeSats and nano satellites, leading to a distinct design philosophy for payloads on these platforms. Quite often, the small payloads for astronomy are designed to address specific science cases that are not possible with larger, more sensitive missions. The development of these payloads demands innovation to address the technological challenges. The Small/Space Payloads group at the Indian Institute of Astrophysics (IIA) has been building UV astronomy instruments suited for short-term (1-2 years) missions on CubeSat platforms. In this presentation, I will summarize a few science cases and the UV astronomy payloads being developed to address them. The design of innovative subsystems for these missions will be discussed, and launch opportunities for science payloads in India will also be covered.

Items.Authors: Hidenori Takahashi, Hiroaki Maezawa, Hiroyuki Hashiba, Hidemi Hishino
Items.Title: Development of near-infrared scanning Fabry-Perot spectrometer for 3D spectroscopy II: improvements to the final model and practical performances for scientific observations
Items.Abstract: We are developing a Fabry-Perot spectrometer for three-dimensional spectroscopic observation in the near-infrared wavelength range. By achieving the interferometric optical elements variable and combining detector module, it can acquire images at arbitrary wavelengths. Since the spectrometer module must operate under vacuum and low temperature, optical elements (etalon), drive actuators (piezo), and displacement sensor systems (capacitive sensor) optimized for that environment were selected. Its compact shape is optimized for use as a front-end optics of imaging module. Furthermore, a control system is developed that maintains high spectroscopic performance by actively controlling the etalons in real time to constantly maintain the parallelism of the interference gap. The approximate spectroscopic specifications are a wavelength resolution of R=6,000 for the finesse = 60 and an order = 100.
